newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW-Malaysia April CPI up 2.6 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Malaysia April CPI up 2.6 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Malaysia's Consumer Price Index (CPI) for April rose 2.6 percent from the same month a year ago, the Statistics Department said on Friday. Following are comments from economists and analysts.
KEVIN CHEW, ECONOMIST WITH CASPIAN SECURITIES:

"I think it's been holding above 3 percent for quite some time so the 2.6 percent number is a bit surprising. A number of factors could be involved. The reduction in import duties over the past few budgets has had an accruing effect on economy. The ringgit has been quite stable. Apart from that, the government has adopted a quite aggressive strategy through price controls and other administrative controls that when combined has kept the lid on inflation."
KOSTAS PANAGIOTOU, SENIOR ECONOMIST AT KIM ENG SECURITIES:

"I would think people were expecting around three percent. If one looks at at the CPI previously, the core CPI has been very low, actually below two pct at around 1.7-1.6. The food component of the CPI was lifting it above three percent. The food component has probably come down.
Normally the market does not react, but this is quite a big drop. We may get some favourable reactions in the market.
The market tends to be sceptical about the reliability of CPI figures. People look at wages and salaries which are in double-digit growth. It is hard to reconcile this with the CPI.
I believe the CPI is reliable because many of the items (in the basket) are controlled (by the government)."
